newsitem.title: USA: Regeneron sees 2-3 candidates by 1998 end.
newsitem.headline: Regeneron sees 2-3 candidates by 1998 end.

text.p: Regeneron Pharmaceutical Inc said on Tuesday that it could have two or three new product candidates in clinical trials by the end of 1998.
The company said that it has over $95 million in cash and cash equivalents and that it believes these funds are adequate to support its clinical and research pipeline for two to three years.

Last week, Regeneron and Amgen Inc said that their Phase III clinical trial of Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) failed to show clinical efficacy in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as Lou Gehrig's disease.
Regeneron and Amgen are in a 50-50 partnership developing Regeneron's BDNF and NT-3 drugs.
Regeneron noted that BDNF is currently being tested by Amgen as a treatment for ALS, delivered directly into the spinal fluid. In the failed trial, the drug was delivered subcutaneously.
Amgen is testing BDNF in two other conditions involving peripheral neurons, as well.
Regeneron is also developing its second generation neurotrophic factor, Axokine for Huntington's disease and retinitis pigmentosa.
